title: Skipper-CCD repeated non-destructive sampling of gain-cell charge
idea: Borrowed from dark-matter Skipper CCDs that measure one charge packet hundreds of times: a gain cell's storage node gates a floating-gate sense transistor that a column-parallel integrator samples 16-64 times without disturbing the charge, averaging noise down by sqrt(N). Cells holding only ~200-500 electrons (0.03-0.08 fF) become reliably readable.
why: Capacitor charge wall (fact 1): required storage charge drops 10-50x, freeing planar or capacitor-less cells from 60-75:1 pillars; cost is ~5-15 ns extra read latency.

title: Particle-detector charge amplifier holds bitline at virtual ground
idea: Like LHC pixel ASICs that read ~1000-electron hits in 25 ns, each sense stripe uses a folded-cascode charge-sensitive amplifier that clamps the bitline at virtual ground and integrates the full cell charge onto a ~1 fF feedback capacitor, so the output is Qcell/Cf instead of Qcell/(Cs+Cbl). Bitline capacitance drops out of the signal equation.
why: Charge wall and periphery area: a signal independent of Cbl lets bitlines be 2-4x longer (2-4x fewer SAs, ~10-15% die saved) or Cs ~3x smaller.

title: CCD charge-transfer bitline segments feeding a tiny sense node
idea: Astronomical CCDs move charge packets with 99.9999% efficiency instead of sharing them; each bitline is split into 8-16 clocked transfer gates that shift the cell's packet to a ~0.3 fF floating diffusion at the SA rather than dumping it onto a 50-100 fF bitline. The SA sees roughly 10x the voltage of conventional charge sharing.
why: Breaks the Cs/Cbl ratio rule behind fact 1: ~10x signal allows ~1 fF cells or 4x longer bitlines; the transfer adds ~3-8 ns.

title: Image-sensor column ADCs with CDS read two bits per cell
idea: Copy 50-megapixel phone sensors that digitize 1-electron-noise columns in parallel: every bitline pair gets a single-slope ADC sharing one global ramp, with correlated double sampling (sample at precharge, again after charge share) to cancel kTC noise and SA offset. Cells store four charge levels for 2 bits/cell.
why: Cost per bit and density up ~1.7-2x without a lithography shrink; refresh must run ~2x more often, partly offset by the CDS margin gain.

title: Lock-in detection of gain-cell current via modulated read wordline
idea: Gravitational-wave and lock-in instruments pull nanovolt signals out of 1/f noise by modulation; the read wordline is toggled at ~2 GHz for 8-10 cycles and the sense amp synchronously demodulates the bitline current with a mixer-integrator, so static offset and 1/f noise of the periphery cancel. Gain cells with read currents of only ~100 nA become sensible.
why: Lets weak, ultra-low-leakage gain cells (refresh-light, fact 3) work without big read transistors; SA offset requirement relaxed ~5x.

title: SiGe HBT preamplifier stage with sub-millivolt offset matching
idea: Nuclear instruments and 200 C downhole electronics prefer bipolars for matching and hardness; insert a SiGe HBT differential pre-amp (behind a MOS source follower so base current never drains the bitline) ahead of the CMOS latch. HBT Vbe mismatch is ~0.3-1 mV versus ~10-15 mV for minimum MOS pairs.
why: Required bitline signal drops from ~100 mV to ~25 mV: Cs can fall ~3x or bitlines grow ~3x longer, attacking facts 1 and 7.

title: LN2 memory pods with 4x wordlines and 2x bitlines
idea: Design a die only for 77 K immersion pods: copper resistivity drops ~6x so each sub-wordline driver can serve 4x more cells, and lower thermal noise plus near-zero leakage allow 2x longer bitlines with a longer sense window. SWD and SA stripes shrink to roughly a third of their usual area.
why: Periphery 49% -> ~25-30% of die, refresh eliminated (fact 3), ~1.4x bits per wafer; cost moves into cryo infrastructure.

title: Twin decaying reference cells written alongside every row
idea: Downhole tools at 200 C see retention collapse to milliseconds; each row carries two reference cells written '1' and '0' at the same instant as its data, and at read they are charge-shared into a mid-level reference that sags exactly as the row's own '1' cells leak. Sensing becomes relative instead of absolute.
why: Refresh interval 2-4x longer at any temperature (fact 3: 16-33% of idle power, 10-20% of bandwidth) for ~0.2% array overhead.

title: Hybrid-bonded GaN HEMT tier for wordline drivers and pumps
idea: GaN, used in space and 200 C power electronics, has ~10x silicon's breakdown field; a thin GaN-on-Si e-mode HEMT tier hybrid-bonded under the array hosts sub-wordline drivers and VPP switches, delivering 3-4 V swings with tiny high-voltage devices instead of thick-oxide silicon.
why: SWD and high-voltage periphery (~10-15% of die) shrink ~3x; higher wordline overdrive and deeper negative wordline cut the leakage tail (fact 3).

title: Leaky-integrator analog counters catch row hammering at activation rate
idea: Design for the extreme user, the attacker: each activation dumps a fixed charge packet onto that row's ~2 fF integrating capacitor in the SWD stripe, which self-leaks with a ~64 ms time constant; a shared comparator checks it on every activation and triggers neighbor refresh past threshold. An analog rate detector replaces SRAM counter tables.
why: Row hammer at ~1k activations (fact 9) tracked for every row with ~0.5% area instead of megabits of counters, and with no counter aliasing.

title: Completion-detecting self-timed sense amps remove worst-case guard bands
idea: Asynchronous circuits built for deep-space radiation and 30-year aging corners signal when they are done; dual-rail SA outputs feed a completion tree per mat that fires column access as soon as every latch has resolved, instead of waiting a fixed tRCD set by the slowest cell at end of life.
why: Typical-case row-to-column latency 20-35% lower; timing margin recovered as bandwidth, so the 49% periphery (fact 7) does more work.

title: Ferroelectric back-gate trim cancels sense-amp offset for 30 years
idea: For 30-year industrial controllers that can never be replaced, each SA transistor pair gets an HZO back-gate whose polarization stores a per-SA threshold trim, programmed at wafer test and re-tuned in the field by a BIST that measures offset. Static mismatch and slow NBTI drift are both nulled.
why: Margin needed falls from ~100 mV to ~30 mV, enabling ~2-3x smaller Cs or longer bitlines, and minimum-size SA devices (facts 1, 7).

title: Ring-oscillator time-domain sensing at 0.4 V array voltage
idea: Energy-harvesting IoT tags have no voltage headroom, so they sense in time: the bitline voltage starves a tiny ring oscillator per column group, and a counter compares its edge count over a fixed window against a reference column. It works at VARY ~0.4 V, where latch SAs fail.
why: Voltage floor (fact 10): bitline CV^2 energy down ~5-6x versus a 1 V VARY; a digital SA scales with logic nodes.

title: Resonant LC tank recovers bitline swing energy adiabatically
idea: Pacemakers count every picojoule: bitline restore is driven by a sinusoidal resonant supply from an on-interposer inductor network, so bitlines charge adiabatically and return their energy to the tank at precharge instead of dumping it to ground.
why: Bitline charging dominates activation energy; 50-70% recovery would cut fact 10's stuck CV^2 per activation ~2x.

title: Frequency-multiplexed wordline group select borrowed from MKID astronomy arrays
idea: MKID cameras read thousands of detectors on one feedline by giving each a unique resonance; each wordline group taps a shared global line through a passive high-Q LC notch tuned to its own frequency, and a tone burst on the line selects that group. Global predecoder wiring collapses to one line per bank.
why: Row-decoder and global wiring area (part of fact 7's 49%) cut sharply; speculative because on-die high-Q resonators are large and slow to ring up.

title: Dual-threshold margin sensing sets each row's own refresh interval
idea: Like event cameras that report only changes: during refresh, a second coarse comparator in each SA stripe flags whether any cell in the row came in below a 'healthy' margin window. Healthy rows skip the next 1-3 refresh rounds; only flagged rows keep the base rate, driven by measured margin instead of a static profile.
why: Refresh operations cut ~60-80% because most cells retain >1 s, recovering fact 3's 10-20% bandwidth; adapts to temperature and aging automatically.

title: Sense amps chain into a shift register for streaming readout
idea: AI KV-caches read whole rows in order, so in streaming mode the SA latches daisy-chain into a shift register clocked out at the mat edge, bypassing column select lines and the column decoder; random access keeps only a coarse 8-way select.
why: Column decoder and CSL area (~5%) shrinks and fact 8's 128x overfetch becomes useful data; streaming energy per bit ~40% lower.

title: Bit-significance-tiered sense amps: big for MSBs, tiny for LSBs
idea: KV-cache and weight tensors tolerate errors in low mantissa bits: columns mapped to sign and exponent bits get large offset-compensated SAs, while LSB columns get minimum-size latches running at ~1e-4 BER with relaxed refresh. The controller fixes the bit-to-column layout.
why: SA area -30% and refresh energy -40% on AI-tier dies (facts 3, 7) with negligible model-accuracy loss.

title: Sample-and-hold capacitors let one sense amp serve eight bitlines
idea: Neural implants and image sensors time-share one converter across many columns; each bitline's post-charge-share voltage is captured on a BEOL MIM sample capacitor above the array, one SA resolves the eight samples in sequence, and a compact per-bitline write-back driver restores each cell.
why: SA count /8 and periphery area -15-20% (fact 7), at the cost of ~10-20 ns longer row cycle.

title: Qubit-style dispersive resonator readout of a varactor storage node
idea: Quantum computers read qubits non-destructively through a tiny shift in resonator frequency; a cell's storage node biases a MOS varactor that loads a shared bitline resonator, and a microwave probe reads the state as a phase shift without discharging the node. Read needs no restore cycle.
why: Removes fact 8's destructive read and restore energy and allows repeated reads of one row; speculative because the per-cell capacitance shift is tiny.

title: SPAD-style avalanche first stage turns electrons into digital pulses
idea: LIDAR single-photon detectors get enormous gain from impact ionization; the SA first stage is an impact-ionization MOSFET biased just below breakdown, so a stored '1' (~1000 electrons) triggers a self-sustaining avalanche that is quenched and reset like a SPAD, while a '0' does not.
why: Gain ~1000x lets ~0.2 fF cells be sensed (fact 1); risks are dark-count false triggers and hot-carrier wear.

title: 4 K cryo-DRAM with single-electron-transistor sensing for qubit controllers
idea: Quantum computers need working memory inside the cryostat: at 4 K leakage is zero and single-electron transistors are practical electrometers, so cells store ~20-50 electrons and an SET coupled to each storage node reads them. Lessons on charge-limit sensing feed room-temperature small-island designs.
why: Refresh-free with ~100x less charge per bit and opens a new cryo-memory niche; generalizing to 300 K is speculative.

title: Fleet-learned per-bank sense timing and voltage from hyperscaler telemetry
idea: Hyperscalers are extreme users with millions of DIMMs: expose per-bank trim registers for tRCD, sense delay, VARY and refresh rate, and let a fleet model trained on correctable-error events and temperature push tuned settings to each die over its life.
why: Recovers ~15-25% latency and energy margin designed for worst-case silicon, and raises usable supply by keeping marginal dies in service.

title: 8K-TV display fabs build slow periphery as IGZO TFTs on glass
idea: With no EUV available, move every non-speed-critical periphery block (fuse banks, repair maps, test logic, refresh counters, power switches) onto an IGZO TFT glass interposer made in depreciated Gen-8.5 display fabs at 1.5-3 um i-line litho, as 8K panels already drive 2 m lines. The silicon die keeps only cells, SAs and fast decoders.
why: Silicon die area -10-15% and capital per m2 ~50-100x lower for those functions; reuses display capacity instead of EUV tools (fact 4).

title: Downhole-grade FD-SOI periphery wafer bonded under array via bitline mux
idea: Without EUV, put SAs and decoders on a 22-65 nm DUV FD-SOI wafer (the substrate downhole and space chips use for heat and radiation) and hybrid-bond it to an array wafer that holds only cells plus an 8:1 bitline select mux, matching ~0.5 um bond pitch to 30-40 nm bitlines. FD-SOI back-bias trims SA offset per mat.
why: Array die gets ~2x bits per mm2 (fact 7) and periphery moves to a cheap DUV node, removing EUV layers from periphery entirely.

title: Nanoimprint templates pattern decoder and sub-wordline-driver stripes
idea: Patterned-media hard drives and RFID makers imprint sub-20 nm features cheaply; the highly regular decoder and SWD stripes are imprinted from a master template at 15-20 nm half-pitch, while irregular logic stays on DUV at relaxed rules.
why: Pitch-critical periphery layers made without EUV at ~1/4 the tool cost (fact 4 capital intensity).

title: Deposition-defined vertical decoder transistors replace lithographic gate lengths
idea: Like MEMS and solar fabs that set critical dimensions by film thickness, decoder transistors are vertical channels whose gate length is an ALD film thickness and whose width is a spacer thickness; logic personalization is done with implants at relaxed DUV pitch.
why: 10 nm-class decoder devices with no EUV, keeping decoder area competitive (facts 4, 7).

title: Randomly doped mesowire decoder with post-fab code discovery
idea: From molecular-electronics crossbars: wordlines are addressed through mesowires whose doping pattern is set stochastically by a self-assembled mask, not lithography; after fab a BIST sweeps address codes, finds which code selects each wordline and stores the map in fuses.
why: Row decoders built without fine lithography, losing ~10-20% of code space to unused codes; attacks fact 4 capital and EUV dependence.

title: DIMM PMIC delivers VPP and VBB, deleting on-die charge pumps
idea: Automotive and industrial boards push high-voltage generation into 180 nm BCD PMICs; DDR5 already moved 12 V to 1.1 V conversion onto the DIMM, so extend it by supplying ~3 V VPP and negative VBB on dedicated balls and deleting on-die pumps (30-40% efficient), keeping only local switches.
why: Die area -5-8% (fact 7) and pump energy ~2x better; the PMICs come from U.S. legacy BCD lines with no EUV.

title: Cool instead of shrink: 77 K lets DUV periphery match EUV
idea: Cryogenic computing users show mobility rises ~2x and leakage vanishes at 77 K; a DRAM whose periphery is built on a DUV-only 28 nm-class process and runs in LN2 pods matches the speed and standby power of an EUV-node room-temperature die.
why: Removes the need for 5-7 EUV layers (fact 4) in periphery and controller, with refresh near zero; trades capex for cryo opex.

title: Self-boosting gain cell drives a plain inverter, no sense amp
idea: $1 IoT chips cannot afford precision analog: a 3T gain cell whose read wordline couples its storage node upward yields a near-rail bitline swing, so a skewed inverter replaces the cross-coupled SA and reference generator, all drawn at relaxed DUV rules.
why: SA area -70% and no offset trimming; periphery simple enough for 40-90 nm U.S. fabs, trading some cell area.

title: Dumb-array DRAM: CXL controller absorbs refresh, ECC, repair, test
idea: Hyperscalers already own smart memory controllers, so strip the DRAM die to cells, SAs, decoders and a narrow I/O; refresh scheduling, row-hammer tracking, ECC, repair remapping, mode registers and BIST move into a CXL controller on a logic node. With no random logic left, the DRAM die needs no EUV.
why: Periphery 49% -> ~30% (fact 7), and the DRAM die can be made in DUV-only fabs.

title: Coincident half-pulse wordline select borrowed from Apollo core memory
idea: Core memories selected a bit where two half-currents met; two half-amplitude pulses launched from opposite ends of a bank-wide transmission line meet at a sub-array chosen by their relative delay, and only there does the sum exceed the local access threshold. Local decoders vanish.
why: Local row decoders removed (fact 7) with no fine litho; speculative because it needs ~10 ps timing precision.

title: Token-ring wordline sequencer for append-only KV-cache mats
idea: KV-caches append and stream tokens in order, so dedicated mats replace the row decoder with a token passed along a chain of shift-register stages (one per 8 wordlines plus a 3-bit local predecoder), allowing random access only at block granularity. Everything is drawn at DUV pitch.
why: Row-decoder area -60% in AI-tier mats with no EUV-pitch decoders, matched to KV-cache access patterns.

title: Voltage-stacked mats recycle bitline charge through series domains
idea: Space and implant power systems stack loads in series: two mats sit between 2 V and ground with a 1 V mid-rail, so charge that discharges the upper mat's bitlines then charges the lower mat's. A scheduler pairs activations to keep the stack balanced.
why: Bitline energy drawn from the supply roughly halved (fact 10), with simpler regulators and only DUV circuitry.

title: Telegraph-style regenerative repeaters halve effective bitline capacitance
idea: Undersea telegraph cables used repeaters to regenerate signals along long spans; a 4-transistor regenerative latch at each bitline's midpoint isolates the far segment, amplifies the near-segment signal, then drives the far segment, so each cell sees half the bitline capacitance.
why: Doubles cells per SA or doubles signal, so relaxed-pitch DUV arrays stay viable with 2x longer bitlines (facts 1, 7).

title: Charge-domain popcount on sense stripes prefilters KV-cache tokens
idea: Store 64-bit locality-sensitive-hash signatures of keys; after sensing, each SA XNORs its bit with a broadcast query bit and dumps a unit charge onto a mat-level summing capacitor, whose voltage (Hamming similarity) one ADC per mat reads. Only top-scoring tokens' full keys leave the chip.
why: KV-cache data movement (fact 5) cut 5-20x for long contexts; analog in-place compute needs no advanced node.

title: Data-polarity rotation balances sense-amp aging over 30 years
idea: Thirty-year industrial parts fail from slow asymmetric drift: the controller inverts stored polarity on alternate refresh epochs (tracked by a per-row flag bit), so both transistors of each SA pair see equal NBTI/PBTI stress and offset stays near zero. SAs can be sized for beginning-of-life margin.
why: SA width ~20% smaller at relaxed DUV rules (fact 7) with no end-of-life guard band.

title: Overclocker-style margin binning routes weak dies into tolerant tiers
idea: Overclockers prove dies vary widely: an on-die SA margin sweeper characterizes every die at test, and dies that miss JEDEC margins are sold into KV-cache and approximate-memory tiers with relaxed refresh and ECC instead of being scrapped. DUV-only dies with wider variation stay economical.
why: Usable supply +5-10% from the same wafers, offsetting the variability penalty of non-EUV processes.

title: Trusted-foundry legacy fabs supply U.S. DRAM periphery dies
idea: Defense programs already fund trusted 90-45 nm U.S. fabs; a policy program pays these lines to make DRAM periphery and base dies (SAs, decoders, I/O) for hybrid bonding to array wafers, backed by offtake guarantees from federal and hyperscaler buyers.
why: U.S. manufacturability: roughly half of DRAM die function made domestically with no EUV, using existing capex.

title: Wired-NOR zero-detect lines suppress all-zero bursts at sense stripes
idea: Satellites downlink only non-trivial data: each SA group pulls down a wired-NOR line if any latched bit is 1, so all-zero 64-byte sectors return a 1-bit flag instead of a full burst over global I/O and pins. Sparse AI activations and zero-padded KV pages benefit most.
why: I/O energy (fact 5) down 20-50% on sparse data with trivial DUV circuitry.

title: Nano vacuum-channel transistors as radiation-proof wordline boost drivers
idea: Nuclear and EMP environments favor vacuum electronics; field-emission vacuum-channel transistors with ~50 nm gaps defined by oxide etch-back rather than lithography switch 3-5 V wordlines with no gate-oxide stress and full immunity to heat and radiation.
why: Shrinks high-voltage SWD devices (fact 7) and lifts the wordline voltage ceiling; emitter reliability is speculative.

title: Lunar-fab materials: molybdenum periphery contacts and helium-free processing
idea: Design periphery for a fab with no tungsten or helium, as on a Moon base: periphery contact plugs and wordline straps use ALD molybdenum or ruthenium instead of W/WF6, and wafer backside cooling uses hydrogen-argon blends instead of helium, all at DUV rules.
why: Removes chokepoints (tungsten ~80% China, Qatari helium offline) from periphery and lowers small-via resistance.

title: Excimer-laser LTPS decoders built monolithically above the cell array
idea: Smartphone OLED backplanes make ~100 cm2/Vs LTPS TFTs by excimer-laser annealing; a laser-crystallized poly-Si layer above the bitlines hosts row decoders and SWD logic at DUV rules, moving them out of the silicon area beside the array.
why: Decoder and SWD area beside the mats (~10% of die) reclaimed without EUV; the laser anneal's thermal budget stays local.

title: NMOS-only bootstrap wordline drivers revive 1970s DRAM tricks
idea: Early DRAM designers had no PMOS and drove wordlines with self-bootstrapped NMOS gates; reusing this, sub-wordline drivers need no PMOS or n-well, which removes well spacing from the SWD stripe and gives a uniform NMOS pitch printable with DUV.
why: SWD stripe area -25-35% (fact 7) and fewer masks.

title: Undersea-cable photonics replace global I/O lines via DUV photonic die
idea: Telecom crosses oceans with WDM light: a 45 nm DUV silicon-photonics die hybrid-bonded to the DRAM carries bank data on SiN waveguides, with microring modulators at each bank edge, replacing long global I/O metal lines and pin SERDES.
why: Data-movement energy (fact 5) toward ~1 pJ/bit and global routing area freed, with no EUV.
